title: TA8-13515
frame:
Forum: Refugee Protection Division (first-instance tribunal).
Parties: the claimant and the Minister; names are redacted.
Decision under review: none; this is the first-instance decision.
How the layers nest here: The member of the tribunal is the author (layer 1). The claimant and the Minister make submissions to the member (layer 2). There is no earlier decision-maker unless the reasons describe a prior decision (layer 3). Testimony and documents are layer 5.

paragraphs.text: These are the reasons I reject the refugee protection claim of, XXXXXXXXXXX, the claimant, a 24-year-old citizen of Albania, who seeks refugee protection pursuant to sections 96 and 97(1) of the Immigration and Refugee Protection Act1(IRPA). ALLEGATIONS:

The claimant alleges that because of a property dispute, his uncle physically assaulted, XXX XXXX, resulting in the declaration of a blood feud. The claimant's father had been away in XXXX, since the late 1990's. His family, including the claimant, followed in 2001.
The claimant's family was informed that the XXX family had discovered their whereabouts and hence, the claimant left XXX, came to Canada and made a claim for refugee protection in 2008.
The claimant notes a cousin, XXXXXXXX, son of XXXXXX, made a successful claim for refugee protection in 2005. DETERMINATION:
The claimant failed to establish the basis of his fear of returning to Albania. Hence, the claim fails. ANALYSIS:

The claimant had status in XXXX, valid until XXXXX 2012. The claimant testified he abandoned his status in XXXX when his father learned from others that the XXXX family had discovered where the claimant and his family were living in XXXX. The balance of the claimant's family continued to live and work in the same area of XXXX after the claimant fled, in 2008. There is no evidence they were ever approached or harassed by the XXXX family or others. The claimant explained his father worked in a secure work site and was very careful. At the first sitting, the claimant testified he was at greater risk because he was the oldest.

If in fact, there is a blood feud in Albania involving honour and the injured family had discovered the location of the claimant's family, I would have expected, according to the code, the XXXX family to take action, to restore their honour. The claimant's father would be in at least, the same danger as his son. Further, if the claimant's father believed the family's whereabouts had been discovered, it would be reasonable to expect that at the very least, he would have moved the family to another area of XXXX.

In addition, there were inconsistencies as to how the family was informed of the danger in XXXX. At the first sitting, the claimant testified his father had been told by his aunt i.e., his father's sister. At the second sitting, the claimant recalled the family learned by word of mouth. In his PIF narrative, the claimant wrote "... my father and I received threats from the XXXX family indirectly. Persons from the same area of Albania passed the word to my father in XXXX ..." The claimant explained he did not mention his paternal aunt because his aunt did not know then (when he wrote the narrative) what was needed or not. I do not accept that the claimant's account of persons from the same area giving information to the claimant and his father is consistent with his aunt telling his father and the father telling the claimant. Further, if the family was informed by the aunt, then I am satisfied this would have been reflected in the straight reading.

Due to the fact the claimant's family has continued to live in the same area of XXXX and the inconsistent evidence as to how the family was informed of the threats, I am satisfied, on a balance of probabilities, the account of the XXXX family having found the family in XXXX was created to advance the claimant's refugee claim.

Counsel submitted that the slap was the cause of the blood feud and the alleged land dispute was only peripheral. I note this is consistent with the PIF narrative at the top of page 2. However, I do not agree. If it was not for the land dispute, there would not have been an incident and without the incident, there would be no blood feud. I am satisfied a finding concerning the land dispute is justified on these facts.

At the second sitting, the claimant testified he did not know how the land became into dispute. He was asked if the land ownership was resolved through government authorities. He did not know. The claimant testified, XXXXX, owned the land since the fall of communists.

The claimant did not know why XXXXXX disputes the ownership. Exhibit C-2, page 45, shows the basis of the dispute was a result of the XXXX family stating his family owned the land before its seizure by the communists. Since this is the claimant's document, I do not accept he would not know the basis of the land dispute.

The land in dispute was seized by the communists but restored to the claimant's family. Exhibit C-2, item 10, page 35, dated XXXXXX, 1993, clearly, awards the land to XXXXXX, the claimant's uncle. The claimant's evidence in his PIF indicates this land had been owned by his grandfather in the past. There is no evidence this award was even disputed by any other family.

Further, there is no evidence that XXXXXX disputed or made application for the land ownership. I am satisfied that if the land is in dispute, the claimant's family would be aware of the basis of the dispute. Further, since it is clear the government agency awarded the land to the family, I find it implausible that the claimant would not have been provided these details, as it was the claimant who provided the documents in Exhibit C-2.

If the family were in a dispute, I would expect the family to report the dispute to the appropriate agency. Similarly, death threats are against the law in Albania and as such, should be reported to the police either local or state.

The English version of the Peace Missionaries letter, attests to the existence of a blood feud, but other than interviewing both families, gives no other information as to why the author believes, a feud exists.

As I have stated in other reasons, if two families state they are in a blood feud, the reconciliation committees, who only interview the families have no way to evaluate if such a feud exists. There are many reasons two families might attest to the existence of a blood feud when that is not the case, i.e., a bribe, a threat or because of friendship. Hence, I give these letters insufficient weight to establish, on their own a blood feud exists.
There is no independent, reliable evidence, such as, a police report to support the existence of a blood feud.

Due to the inconsistent evidence concerning the basis of the land dispute and the lack of reliable evidence to establish the blood feud or the land dispute, I am satisfied, the existence of a feud and the land dispute were created to advance this claim.

As a result of my credibility concerns, I am satisfied, on a balance of probabilities, the claimant was not a credible witness. Further, the claimant failed to establish, that for him, there is a serious possibility he will be persecuted or suffer other forms of serious harm should he return to Albania today. CONCLUSION:

Hence, The Refugee Protection Division rejects the claim pursuant to both sections 96 and 97 of the Immigration and Refugee Protection Act. (signed) "Cliff Berry" Cliff Berry July 26, 2011 Date REFUGEE PROTECTION DIVISION / VENDETTA / REVENGE / INCONSISTENCY / CREDIBILITY / MALE / NEGATIVE / ALBANIA 1 As enacted by S.C. 2001, c. 27. --------------- ------------------------------------------------------------ --------------- ------------------------------------------------------------ RPD.15.7 (February 12, 2009) Disponible en français RPD.15.7 (February 12, 2009) Disponible en français RPD File No. : TA8-13515 RPD File No. :TA8-13515
